candidate.title: 2b-RAD
candidate.scope: The supplied Illumina 2b-RAD schematic: a single genomic-DNA-to-library route using type IIB digestion with BsaXI as the shown example, compatible-adapter ligation, initial amplification, and sample-specific barcode incorporation/final amplification. The matching collection page is headed 2b-RAD: RAD With Type IIB Restriction Endonucleases. The left Genome and BsaXI restriction sites illustrations establish substrate and target-site distribution; three parallel molecule icons depict representative tags, not independent branches. Orange terminal segments mark restriction-compatible adapters; differently colored terminal additions mark sample-specific adapters; the endpoint is DNA. This record describes the standard NNN-overhang BsaXI Illumina implementation within 2b-RAD, not every member of the broader family. AlfI, selective RTR libraries, ddRAD, SOLiD and the associated commercial kit are not additional depicted target workflows. Sequencing and genotype analysis are the intended downstream readout, not additional drawn operations.

features: DNA is both the starting chemical substrate and source of the genetic variation to be sampled.

states.label: Type IIB restriction-generated genomic DNA tags

Three short blue lines are representative tag molecules, not three separate workflow branches.

states.label: Sample-barcoded amplified DNA sequencing library
features: DNA library molecules carry restriction-derived genomic tag inserts and library adapter sequences, with PCR-incorporated sample barcodes.

operations.label: Restriction digestion with type IIB restriction endonucleases e.g. BsaXI
operations.description: Genomic DNA is cut upstream and downstream of type IIB recognition sites, generating the short uniform-length genomic tags illustrated in blue. BsaXI is the depicted example; the illustration follows these tags rather than enumerating every digestion coproduct.
operations.mechanism: Type IIB restriction endonuclease cleavage on both sides of the recognition site; BsaXI is a catalyst/reagent of this operation, not a material branch.
operations.information_effect: Defines the genomic loci represented by the tag library and retains the recognition-site region and its flanking sequence; sequence outside the represented tags is not the library readout.

operations.label: Add restriction-site-specific adapters
operations.description: Compatible library adapters are joined to the restriction-generated tags. The blue genomic inserts acquire orange terminal adapter segments. The primary paper identifies cohesive-end ligation of partially double-stranded NNN-overhang adapters for the standard BsaXI implementation.
operations.mechanism: Cohesive-end adapter ligation; the degenerate NNN overhangs accommodate the compatible BsaXI tag ends.
operations.information_effect: Retains each genomic tag as the information carrier while providing the interfaces for subsequent library PCR. NNN denotes overhang degeneracy, not a sample barcode.

operations.label: Add sample-specific adapters; Amplify
operations.description: Sample-specific barcode-bearing primers act on the first-PCR tag templates. The final PCR incorporates those barcode/adapter sequences while amplifying the library, producing the DNA library shown at the right. This local stage accounts for both the Add sample-specific adapters caption and the last Amplify caption.
operations.mechanism: Primary-paper-supported barcode incorporation by PCR using platform-specific barcode-bearing primers; the two schematic captions are represented as one barcode-PCR transformation.
operations.information_effect: Adds a physical sample identity to the genomic-tag-bearing DNA library molecules for multiplex sequencing. Genotyping reads the genomic inserts; sample identity is supplied by the barcode, rather than by the restriction-site adapter or its degenerate overhang.

method_scopes.rationale: All four local transformations belong to the single 2b-RAD route named by the card and diagram. The paper describes the corresponding BsaXI Illumina adapter preparation and sequential initial and barcode PCR stages. The final two source captions denote barcode addition and amplification within one paper-supported barcode-PCR stage; neither caption is omitted. NNN-overhang ligation is interpreted as the standard BsaXI capture architecture. Unshown AlfI and selective-adapter preparations do not inherit this local implementation solely from the family name. No pooling operation is asserted because the drawn route has no merge and the primary preparation text specifies initial amplification per sample.

corrections.diagram_observation: After the first Amplify arrow, the drawing shows orange-adapter-bearing blue tags with additional magenta, green or dark blue terminal segments under Add sample-specific adapters. A following arrow is also labeled Amplify. Thus the colored intermediate is depicted before the last amplification arrow; the drawing does not specify the chemistry of attaching those sample-specific sequences.
corrections.primary_statement: Figure 1 identifies incorporation of multiplex barcodes by PCR; Online Methods specifies initial amplification of ligation products and then final barcode introduction by PCR with platform-specific barcode-bearing primers. The unbarcoded first-PCR boundary s_amplified is authored from that text, whereas the drawing compresses initial amplification and sample-specific addition into its colored intermediate. The colored segments and both source captions are retained as observations. Operation op_barcode_amplify explicitly combines barcode addition and final amplification into the paper-supported barcode PCR; it does not posit a separate sample-adapter ligation or a third PCR.
